topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, contextualises the lecture within the pathology course, and outlines the primary learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Genetic, environmental, and epidemiological factors in cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the core concepts of cancer development by examining how endogenous mutations, inherited predispositions, environmental exposures, and geographic variations shape overall cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious agents and oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the oncogenic mechanisms of infectious pathogens and illustrate them with the multi-factorial viral etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical, dietary, and physical carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how specific physical, dietary, and environmental chemical exposures cause DNA damage directly or via xenobiotic metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host susceptibility, and carcinogenesis mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics differentiate tumor promoters from direct mutagens, exploring how chronic inflammation, cellular signaling, host developmental stage, and tissue context facilitate tumor development.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the primary genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro scientific methodologies used to detect and evaluate carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with summary remarks reflecting on everyday decisions balancing carcinogenic risk against practical benefits.
